name: Karnataka Bank Ltd
title: Karnataka Bank Ltd - 532652 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Karnataka Bank Q2 FY27 PAT rose 4% QoQ to INR435.89 crores, with gross NPA down to 2.27% and aggregate business at a record INR2,07,132 crores.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 showed sequential gains across most metrics: PAT up 4% QoQ to INR435.89 crores, NII up 5% QoQ to INR982.44 crores, and cost-to-income down to 52.68% from 55.14%. Gross NPA fell 31 bps QoQ to 2.27% and slippage eased to 0.11%. NIM dipped to 3.17% from 3.20% in Q1, which management attributed to averaging effects and a one-off income-tax-related item in Q1. Advances grew 6% QoQ and 25% YoY, led by the retail, agri and MSME (RAM) book. Management reiterated FY27 growth guidance of 15% to 20% in advances and 10% to 15% in liabilities.

segments.name: Retail, agri and MSME (RAM)
segments.commentary: RAM book rose 7% QoQ to INR56,968 crores and 19% YoY; about INR3,598 crores added to retail in Q2 across MSME, housing, gold, agri and car loans. RAM is 56% of the advances mix.

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: IBPC book fell to INR1,309 crores from INR1,375 crores, with about INR66 crores replaced by higher-yielding loans. Mix is mid-corporate 20% and large corporate 24%, with large corporate targeted to fall to 18%.

segments.name: Deposits
segments.commentary: Retail term deposits under INR3 crores rose 4% QoQ to INR72,197 crores and 10% YoY. Bulk deposits are being reduced in favour of granular retail deposits.

guidance_outlook: NIM guided to 3% to 3.4% range, with management saying it will be at the upper end of that range; no separate H2 NIM number given.
ROA guidance of 1.1% to 1.35% (stated as 1.1% plus, or 1.1% to 1.3%).
Advances growth of 15% to 20% for the year (translates to about 18% to 19% YoY average, per management), and liabilities growth of 10% to 15%.
AOP business target of INR83,000 crores to INR98,000 crores; about INR15,000 crores added in H1 leaves about INR18,000 crores for H2.
Branch expansion: at least 15 branches before December 2026 and 31 branches in FY27, with a stated ambition to cross 1,000 branches this financial year.
Mix targets: retail from 56% to 60%, mid-corporate from 20% to 22%, large corporate from 24% to 18%.
Management expects a major recovery of one or two accounts and a big recovery number in Q3 FY27.
ECL transition from 1 April 2027 could cost 1% to 1.75% of capital; the hit may be spread over 5 years, and management said the impact will fall as stress declines.
capex_capacity: Branch network: about 24 centres finalised with premises fixed and 17 under construction (safe room, interiors); at least 15 branches to open before December 2026 and 31 in FY27.

IT spend: management said a couple of major IT investments are budgeted for FY27; of every INR100 invested, 40% to 50% goes to licences and upgrades, 20% to 25% to regulatory compliance, and 25% to 30% to business.
Live digital solutions include digitised gold loans, interest-bearing credit lines on UPI, SD-WAN, a common data platform, Mule Hunter and the Sales Buddy AI assistant.
In progress: loan against mutual funds, shares on digital channel, secured credit cards, DPDP solution, new treasury application and new NPA management solution.
demand_pricing: Loan yield on advances rose 8 bps QoQ to 8.76%; cost of funds was 5.15% vs 5.16% in Q1, a 1 bp improvement.
Around 70% of the advances book is EBLR or T-bill linked, with MCLR about 5%; management said assets reprice within about 3 months, while liabilities reprice more slowly.
Management said rates have bottomed out and the October policy repo hike to 5.50% (25 bps) will feed into asset yields over the next quarter or so.
CD ratio rose to 79.93% from 78.45% in Q1 and 71.63% in Sep 2025.
Fee income was flat YoY at about INR206 to INR207 crores; management attributed the moderation to Q1 locker income and Q4 card income being one-offs.

qa_highlights.question: Will NIM move to the upper end of the 3% to 3.4% range, and what is the H2 ROA outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated NIM of 3% to 3.4% and ROA of 1.1% to 1.3%, citing a 3 bps QoQ dip driven by averaging and a Q1 income-tax item. It gave no separate H2 NIM number.

qa_highlights.question: Why was provisioning not more aggressive given the West Asia conflict and inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said PCR rose to 68.05% from 67.03% and is ahead of its commitment of about 1% per quarter; it said provisioning is kept at the best level allowed by audit and internal strength.

qa_highlights.question: Will the bank reach 1,000 branches this financial year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H1 was slow due to premises rent discipline. It expects 15 or more branches before December and 31 in FY27, and said it aims to cross 1,000 branches this year.

qa_highlights.question: Why is fee income flat YoY despite higher disbursements?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 locker and Q4 card income are one-offs, and that new fee lines (mutual fund platform, loans against shares, credit cards) are being rolled out. It said flat income is unacceptable.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the advances book is T-bill linked and when will the October T-bill spike reach asset yields?
qa_highlights.answer: About 70% is EBLR, with the rest mostly T-bill linked, and MCLR about 5%. Management expects the repricing to flow through in December and January within about 3 months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected ECL transition impact, and what is the outlook for drought-related agri stress?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated a 1% to 1.75% capital impact from 1 April 2027 and said the hit may be spread over 5 years. On drought, it said it is monitoring closely and sees no immediate serious problem.

risks_watch: ECL transition from 1 April 2027 could cost 1% to 1.75% of capital; the spread-over option and final impact are still under study.
Drought in parts of the country may pressure the agri and gold book; management says no serious issue is visible yet.
Treasury: the G-Sec and tenure hardening may affect the investment portfolio; management said the HFT book is small relative to INR27,000 crores of investments.
Fee income momentum is weak: flat YoY, and the new fee lines are still in implementation.
Branch expansion depends on 31 openings by 31 March 2027, with 15 due before December.
summary.management_tone: Confident on headline growth, asset quality and the Q3/Q4 outlook, but vague on specifics; management repeatedly deferred numbers ("kindly wait and watch") on recoveries, fee income and H2 NIM. It was defensive on the flat fee income and the NIM dip.
key_quotes: Before December end, we will be adding minimum 15 branches.
Flat income cannot be accepted at all.
Right now, we are in retail 56%, mid-corporate 20%, large 24%.

adds.what: Branch expansion: at least 15 branches before Dec 2026 and 31 branches in FY27 (about 24 centres finalised, 17 under construction)

growth.why: Management held FY27 advances growth guidance at 15-20% and liabilities at 10-15%, with business growth around 15%; Q2 advances grew 25% YoY and the AOP target of INR83,000-98,000 crores implies about INR18,000 crores more in H2, backed by 31 branches planned in FY27 and mostly partial specifics rather than capacity or contracts with numbers.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: NIM at 3.17% (down 3 bps from 3.20%) with guidance of 3% to 3.4% and management saying it will be at the upper end; October 25 bps repo hike to 5.50% flows into asset yields over about 3 months, but ~70% EBLR/T-bill-linked assets reprice faster than liabilities, and cost-to-income is guided down to 51%-52% from 52.68%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: At least 15 branches before December 2026 and 31 in FY27, with about 24 centres finalised and 17 under construction; management is confident all 31 open before 31 March 2027.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Advances grew 6% QoQ and 25% YoY to INR92,015 crores, and FY27 guidance of 15%-20% advances growth needs about INR18,000 crores more business in H2 against INR15,000 crores in H1.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex discussed only as branch openings and IT budget; no utilisation or plant capacity data given, so no new capex announcement is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held advances (15%-20%) and liabilities (10%-15%) guidance and deferred H2 NIM numbers, so no upgrade is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: ROA guidance was cut to 1.1%-1.3% (from 1.29% QoQ in Q2 and 1.26% actual), fee income is flat YoY at about INR206-207 crores, and a 1%-1.75% ECL capital hit arrives from 1 April 2027.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Loan against mutual funds, shares on digital channel, secured credit cards, DPDP solution and new treasury and NPA applications are in progress, and management says new fee lines are being rolled out to lift fee income that is flat YoY.

rows.label: Major recovery of one or two accounts in Q3 FY27
rows.why: Management expects a big recovery number in Q3 FY27, but deferred specifics ('kindly wait and watch'), and gross NPA is already down to 2.27% from 3.33% a year ago with PCR at 68.05%.

rows.label: Shift from bulk to granular retail deposits
rows.why: Retail term deposits under INR3 crores rose 4% QoQ to INR72,197 crores, and bulk deposits are being cut; CASA ratio still slipped to 31.80% from 32.42%, so funding cost pressure may persist.

rows.label: ECL transition from 1 April 2027
rows.why: Estimated capital hit of 1%-1.75% with a 5-year spread option under study; CRAR already fell to 20.36% from 21.10% in June 2026.

tone.note: Management was confident on headline growth, asset quality, the 31-branch plan and the Q3 recovery, but vague on fee income, H2 NIM and recoveries, and defensive on the flat fee income and the NIM dip; analysts pushed on NIM, provisioning versus the West Asia and inflation risk, and branch pace.
